# Page templates

> Plainkit 0.1.0-alpha.1. Generated by scripts/build-skills.mjs from core/samples/templates and the element API. Do not edit: change the source and run the generator.

Full-page starting points, one folder each in `dist/gallery/templates/<id>/`. The markup below is the page content (the demo pages put it inside `<main id="content">`, or use a `pk-workspace` with that id); the demo pages wrap it in a demo shell (`chrome.js`), which you should not copy: build your own frame from `pk-app-shell` with `pk-side-nav` or `pk-navbar` (see `elements-navigation.md`, and the `overlays-nav` template, which shows one). To start from a template: put its markup in your page, keep the page script if one is shown (it is what the demo runs after the shell; its imports assume `plainkit/` is a copy of `dist` next to your page), and change the text and data.

## page: Page

Breadcrumbs, title with optional back button, page actions, content, footer.

Elements used: `pk-button` `pk-card` `pk-field-list` `pk-stack`.

```html
<pk-stack>
<pk-card heading="Content"><p>The page template is breadcrumbs, a title with an optional back button (both in the top bar), page actions, content and a footer. Content goes in cards or any block inside the container.</p><p class="muted">Slots: crumbs, title, actions, content, footer.</p></pk-card>
<pk-card heading="Another block"><pk-field-list><dt>Name</dt><dd>Item one</dd><dt>Status</dt><dd>Active</dd><dt>Created</dt><dd>Sep 12</dd><dt>Amount</dt><dd>$12.00</dd></pk-field-list></pk-card>
</pk-stack>
```

## workspace: Workspace

A nav rail, one tab strip over a content pane and a docked inspector. Fills the viewport; rail and pane scroll on their own.

Elements used: `pk-button` `pk-field-list` `pk-input` `pk-stack` `pk-tab` `pk-tab-panel` `pk-tabs` `pk-toolbar` `pk-tree` `pk-tree-item` `pk-workspace`.

```html
<pk-workspace id="content" fill nav-label="List" main-label="Content" aside-label="Inspector">
  <pk-stack slot="nav" gap="sm">
    <pk-input type="search" label="Filter the list" placeholder="Filter the list"></pk-input>
    <pk-tree label="Items"><pk-tree-item label="Group" expanded><pk-tree-item label="First item" selected></pk-tree-item><pk-tree-item label="Second item"></pk-tree-item></pk-tree-item></pk-tree>
  </pk-stack>
  <pk-tabs value="one" scroll>
    <pk-tab value="one" closable>First item</pk-tab>
    <pk-tab value="two">Second item</pk-tab>
    <pk-button slot="trailing" id="inspector-toggle" toggle variant="ghost" size="mini">Inspector</pk-button>
    <pk-tab-panel value="one"><pk-stack><h2>First item</h2><p>The pane shows what the active tab selects.</p><pk-field-list><dt>Name</dt><dd>Item one</dd><dt>Status</dt><dd>Active</dd><dt>Created</dt><dd>Sep 12</dd><dt>Amount</dt><dd>$12.00</dd></pk-field-list></pk-stack></pk-tab-panel>
    <pk-tab-panel value="two"><p>Second item content.</p></pk-tab-panel>
  </pk-tabs>
  <pk-stack slot="aside" gap="sm"><pk-toolbar heading="Inspector"><pk-button id="inspector-close" slot="actions" size="mini" variant="plain" icon label="Close inspector">&#10005;</pk-button></pk-toolbar><p class="muted">A docked inspector covers the pane, not the page.</p></pk-stack>
</pk-workspace>
```

Page script:

```js
// The inspector is the workspace's docked aside; its toggle and its close button keep asideOpen and the pressed state together.
const workspace = document.getElementById('content');
const toggle = document.getElementById('inspector-toggle');
toggle.addEventListener('pk-toggle', e => { workspace.asideOpen = e.detail.pressed; });
document.getElementById('inspector-close').addEventListener('click', () => { workspace.asideOpen = false; toggle.pressed = false; });

// Closing a tab removes it and its panel; the strip then selects a neighbour.
const tabs = document.querySelector('pk-tabs');
tabs.addEventListener('pk-tab-close', e => {
    const tab = e.target.closest('pk-tab');
    const panel = tabs.querySelector('pk-tab-panel[value="' + tab.value + '"]');
    const all = [...tabs.querySelectorAll('pk-tab')];
    const neighbour = all[all.indexOf(tab) + 1] ?? all[all.indexOf(tab) - 1];
    tab.remove(); panel?.remove();
    if (neighbour) tabs.value = neighbour.value;
});
```

## wizard: Wizard

A stepper, one card per step, Back and Next.

Elements used: `pk-button` `pk-card` `pk-field` `pk-grid` `pk-input` `pk-stack` `pk-step` `pk-stepper` `pk-toolbar`.

```html
<pk-stack>
<pk-stepper label="Wizard" current="1" clickable><pk-step heading="Step one"></pk-step><pk-step heading="Step two"></pk-step><pk-step heading="Review"></pk-step></pk-stepper>
<pk-card id="step-card" heading="Step two"><pk-grid min="16rem"><pk-field label="Field"><pk-input value="Value"></pk-input></pk-field><pk-field label="Other field"><pk-input></pk-input></pk-field></pk-grid></pk-card>
<pk-toolbar><pk-button id="back" slot="actions" variant="ghost">Back</pk-button><pk-button id="next" slot="actions">Next</pk-button></pk-toolbar>
</pk-stack>
```

Page script:

```js
// The stepper, the card title and the Back and Next buttons stay in step: the elements do the rest.
const titles = ['Step one', 'Step two', 'Review'];
const stepper = document.querySelector('pk-stepper');
const card = document.getElementById('step-card');
const back = document.getElementById('back');
const next = document.getElementById('next');
function update(n) {
    card.heading = titles[n];
    back.disabled = n === 0;
    next.disabled = n === titles.length - 1;
}
function show(n) { stepper.current = n; update(n); }
back.addEventListener('click', () => show(stepper.current - 1));
next.addEventListener('click', () => show(stepper.current + 1));
// A click on a reached step: the event fires before the stepper moves, so it carries the target index.
stepper.addEventListener('pk-step-change', e => update(e.detail.index));
show(stepper.current);
```

Page script:

```js
import { loadElements, observeElements } from './plainkit/js/loader.js';
import { setTheme } from './plainkit/js/theme.js';
setTheme(document.documentElement, new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('theme') === 'light' ? 'light' : 'dark');
loadElements(document);
observeElements(document);
```

Page script:

```js
// Wiring for the overlays and navigation sample: the elements do the work; this only connects the demo buttons to their public API
// (show/hide, the palette's items property) and to the toast helper. Nothing here is needed by the components themselves.
// The overlay elements install the data-open / data-toggle / data-close openers themselves (js/invokers.js).
// The element loader (js/element.js) registers the pk-* tags on demand when the page uses them.

import { loadElements, observeElements } from './plainkit/js/loader.js';
import Toast from './plainkit/elements/toast-stack.js';

loadElements(document);
observeElements(document);
globalThis.PkToast = Toast;

const $ = selector => document.querySelector(selector);

document.addEventListener('click', event => {
    const toaster = event.target.closest('[data-toast]');
    if (toaster) globalThis.PkToast?.show('Draft saved.', { kind: toaster.getAttribute('data-toast'), heading: 'Saved', action: { label: 'Undo' } });
});

const palette = $('#palette');
if (palette) {
    // `items` is a property: set it once the element is defined, or the upgrade would leave it shadowed.
    await customElements.whenDefined('pk-command-palette');
    palette.items = [
        { id: 'dash', label: 'Go to Dashboard', group: 'Navigate', href: '#' },
        { id: 'orders', label: 'Go to Orders', group: 'Navigate', href: '#', keywords: 'sales' },
        { id: 'products', label: 'Go to Products', group: 'Navigate', href: '#', keywords: 'catalog inventory' },
        { id: 'new-po', label: 'New purchase order', group: 'Create', shortcut: 'N' },
        { id: 'new-product', label: 'New product', group: 'Create' },
        { id: 'theme', label: 'Toggle dark theme', group: 'Settings' },
    ];
}
```
